item.text: {"question_id":"4B.9","answer":"For 2023, the supplied evidence does not establish spyware procurement, targeted interception, surveillance-data access, or a nationwide internet shutdown; one assessment reported that authorities did not restrict or disrupt internet access or censor online content. [BATCH-0011-E011] It does, however, document legal and administrative practices that constrained political and digital expression. The revised press law retained possible prison sentences for press offenses and added a bad-faith clause concerning false information or allegations disturbing public order; the Digital Code created prison penalties for disseminating false information online. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0011-E011] Authorities detained journalists over reporting on alleged intelligence facilities, articles, tweets, or online criticism, and ANR agents retained one journalist’s phone intending to search it. [BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0026-E011] Bujakera was arrested, charged under the Digital Code, press law, and penal code, held in pretrial detention, and transferred to prison over a report he allegedly did not author; Tshisekedi said he would not intervene, which indicates a stated separation-of-powers position but does not demonstrate effective oversight or remedy. [BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0025-E013] During election coverage, CSAC ordered Perfect Télévision off air after reports about delayed polling-station openings and missing electoral materials, while party supporters attacked journalists; the supplied evidence does not establish that Tshisekedi personally ordered or endorsed either incident. [BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E003] Authorities also prohibited an opposition march contesting the election and deployed police and armored vehicles to prevent gatherings. [BATCH-0021-E009] More broadly, Tshisekedi’s administration repeatedly extended the state of siege, transferred civilian administration to military and police officials, suspended elected provincial assemblies, and used military courts for civilians; Amnesty linked the resulting framework to harassment and detention of journalists, activists, critics, and political figures. [BATCH-0012-R03-E001, BATCH-0012-R03-E002, BATCH-0012-R03-E003] The planned Goma operation against a banned protest involved killings, arrests, and disputed casualty figures; Amnesty attributed planning and command responsibility to regional military officials, not personally to Tshisekedi, while reporting incomplete accountability. [BATCH-0011-E018, BATCH-0011-E020, BATCH-0011-E011] Thus, the specific surveillance and shutdown mechanisms in the question remain largely unproven, but the 2023 record supports a broader pattern of laws, regulator action, security-force conduct, and administrative restrictions that suppressed political expression and related freedoms, with incomplete evidence of presidential personal direction or effective correction.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E002","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E020"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0021-E012","BATCH-0025-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence establishes spyware procurement, targeted interception, surveillance-data access, or a nationwide internet shutdown.","Reported lack of internet restriction or online censorship does not establish broad digital freedom or lawful surveillance oversight.","Most incidents are attributed to agencies, regulators, security forces, local officials, or party supporters rather than directly to Tshisekedi.","The state-of-siege framework and appointments are attributed to Tshisekedi’s administration, but individual responsibility for each abuse is not established.","The Goma casualty figures and some responsibility accounts remain disputed; investigations and remedies were incomplete or unverified.","The supplied evidence does not establish whether Perfect Télévision’s shutdown or attacks on journalists were later remedied.","Tshisekedi’s stated non-intervention in Bujakera’s case is evidence of a claimed separation-of-powers stance, not proof of effective judicial independence or oversight."],"corrections_made":["Removed any implication that BATCH-0010-E013 supported the Goma operation; that item concerns arrests and detention of critics, journalists, activists, and political figures.","Added the omitted January journalist detentions, April detentions and threatened arrest, phone retention, the full Perfect Télévision timing and stated basis, and the prohibited post-election opposition march.","Separated evidence of digital-expression criminalization and administrative/media suppression from the unproven claims of spyware, interception, surveillance-data use, or nationwide shutdown.","Preserved the distinction between presidential or administrative attribution and personal presidential ordering or endorsement.","Retained contrary evidence concerning non-intervention, no reported internet disruption, consultation-related positive elements in the press-law revision, and government assistance to one attacked journalist."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
